how_to_mine: Follow this plan exactly. Each lens agent reads only its pages (all are in the corpus; read them with `show <source_id> --around TEXT` or `--lines A:B`, tables with `tables <source_id>`), answers its demand items, and records each item as filled (fact ids), contradicted (what the page says instead) or not-found (where you looked). Never refresh or re-fetch a cached page (a refresh changes snapshots that verified facts quote). A page that is not in the corpus may be fetched once (brief `fetch_on_demand`).

Write facts in files of 10 to 25 facts: _build/work/37-monitoring/facts-<lens>-NN.json (lens file names: numbers, behavior, faq), then `facts add --file <that file> --by mine-37-<lens>`. Table rows and value lines: prefer `facts adopt` (--table/--row, --sentence, --heading). Every quote is copied verbatim from the page snapshot (.txt), never from full.md (full.md hits are pointers) and never from memory.

Each quote must carry every clause, scope, condition and exception of the claim on its own. When the condition stands in the next sentence (for example 'This quota cannot be increased.' in a CloudTrail quota cell, 'Data events are not logged by default' next to the definition of data events, or the Region scope of the billing metric), include that sentence in the quote; otherwise narrow the claim. Entail votes run on Opus and mark a clause found only in the surrounding text as partial.

Fact service keys and id prefixes: `cloudwatch` for CloudWatch and CloudWatch Logs facts (ids start with `cloudwatch-`; Logs facts with `cloudwatch-logs-`), `cloudtrail` (ids `cloudtrail-`), `x-ray` (ids `x-ray-`), `health-dashboard` (ids `health-dashboard-`), `managed-grafana` (ids `managed-grafana-`), `managed-prometheus` (ids `managed-prometheus-`). Decision-guide and whitepaper facts go under the service they decide about (CloudTrail-vs-CloudWatch rows under `cloudtrail`, monitoring-guide rows under `cloudwatch`, unless the row is about Grafana or Prometheus). Well-Architected facts for this chapter go under `cloudwatch` (REL06, OPS04, OPS08) or `cloudtrail` (SEC04).

Neighbour facts already exist (n-neighbours.txt: Config vs CloudTrail, organization trail, GuardDuty, EventBridge, S3 Object Lock and access logs, SQS metrics, EC2 Auto Scaling target tracking and step scaling, Route 53 health checks, Lambda, API Gateway and Step Functions X-Ray, VPC Flow Logs). Run `facts list --service <key>` before adding a fact about those services; reuse the existing id in the demand record; never add a second fact with the same claim. No cloudwatch, cloudtrail or x-ray fact existed at plan time.

Every hard fact (number, limit, default, price, date, can/cannot, only/always/never) carries `question` (the demand question it answers) and at least two displays for kinds behavior, capability, restriction and default (brief gate B12). A display of a number-free fact is a verbatim phrase of at most 8 words from its quote (RULINGS 2026-10-11).

Names: write claims with the current names (AWS Health Dashboard, Amazon Data Firehose, Amazon EventBridge, IAM Identity Center, Amazon OpenSearch Service). Where a quote says 'Personal Health Dashboard', 'CloudWatch Events', 'Kinesis Data Firehose' or 'AWS SSO', keep the quote as is; the writer handles 'formerly'.

Changes: a fact touched by a change item sets `changed` (date, old value only if a saved page states it verbatim) and `change_items`. Current truth comes from the guide, quota and pricing pages; What's New pages and history rows give dates and deltas only. A feature GA after 2026-07-15 gets the note `not examinable yet`: CloudWatch Omni (2026-09-23), alarm warm-up periods (2026-09-01), wall clock evaluation windows (2026-08-07), CloudTrail network activity events filtered by identity (2026-07-20), CloudTrail Event Coverage (2026-09-30), Managed Service for Prometheus 1.5B active metrics (2026-07-21), Grafana 13.2 workspaces (2026-09-30), AWS Health version catalog (2026-10-02).
Case-study facts have kind `case-study` and a quote of at most 25 words.

numbers+changes.job: Every number, limit, default and price of CloudWatch (metrics, alarms, dashboards, Logs), CloudTrail and X-Ray, plus 3 to 5 numbers each for the cards (Managed Service for Prometheus, Managed Grafana, AWS Health): the CloudWatch quota table (table 0 of cloudwatch_limits) and the CloudWatch Logs quota page first, then the metric retention list and resolution pages, the alarm limits page, the CloudTrail quota page, the X-Ray General Reference quotas, the four pricing pages (dimensions and units; prefer dimension facts over Regional dollar values), then one change fact per change item in d013, d014, d015 and d016 with the date from the What's New page, the change-feed row or the doc-history row, and a pointer to the current-truth fact. Kinds: limit, quota, default, price, change.
tools: show docs/awscloudtrail/latest/userguide/cloudtrail-document-history --around "no longer be open to new customers"
watch: CloudWatch quota table rows carry a Description column with conditions (per Region, per account, adjustable or not): adopt the row with its header so 'Adjustable' and the scope stay in the quote.

Log event size (d006): the CloudWatch Logs quota row says 1,024 Kilobytes (current truth; changed from 256 KB on 2025-04-02 per the What's New page). The CloudTrail quota page still says 'Amazon CloudWatch Logs and Amazon EventBridge each allow a maximum event size of 256 KB': that sentence is evidence for the CloudTrail delivery rule (events over 256 KB are not sent to CloudWatch Logs or EventBridge), never for the CloudWatch Logs limit. Record the disagreement in the d006 note.

Metric retention (d002) is a bullet list under the heading 'Metrics retention' on cloudwatch_concepts: use `facts adopt --heading` per line, or one fact that quotes the whole list. 'Metrics cannot be deleted, but they automatically expire after 15 months if no new data is published to them' is a separate sentence on the same page.

Basic vs detailed monitoring (d001): say which services the 5-minute and 1-minute statements are about (EC2 in the page's table); other services publish at their own intervals (per-service facts exist, n-neighbours.txt). Detailed monitoring is charged: quote the pricing or the page sentence that says so; do not infer it.

CloudTrail quotas (d010): every row says 'This quota cannot be increased.' inside the Comments cell; keep it. The 90-day event history covers management events in one Region: keep both scopes ('management events', 'in an AWS Region').

CloudTrail pricing (d011): 'first copy of management events free' holds per Region and for trails; additional copies and data events are charged. Quote the pricing-page sentence with that scope; FAQ #95 gives the one-trail-all-Regions answer.

Pricing numbers vary by Region and change often: prefer dimension facts (what is charged and its unit; free-tier contents) over per-unit dollar values; a price fact names the Region the page shows. X-Ray prices are on the CloudWatch pricing page.

What's New URL paths can carry an earlier month than the post date (warm-up: path 2026/08, post 2026-09-01; wall clock: path 2026/07, post 2026-08-07): take the date from the page text or the change-feed row, never from the path.

OpenTelemetry metrics (d003, d016): the guide marks them 'Recommended' and the Classic metrics as 'CloudWatch Metrics (Classic)'. Query Studio with PromQL went GA on 2026-06-15 (preview 2026-04-03): examinable by the date rule but new; the writer puts it in 'Changed recently'. Do not rewrite classic PutMetricData facts as OTel facts.

X-Ray SDK timeline (d013): take maintenance-mode and end-of-support dates from xray-sdk-daemon-timeline; the doc-history rows give when the notice was added. Do not write that X-Ray itself is retired.

behavior+decisions.job: Every behaviour, capability, restriction, default and decision rule the exam uses: CloudWatch concepts, default EC2 metrics vs the CloudWatch agent, custom metrics and the embedded metric format, alarm states, evaluation, missing data and actions (SNS, EC2, Auto Scaling, EventBridge), composite alarms, scaling on metrics (CloudWatch side only), dashboards, billing alarm, cross-account observability and centralization, CloudWatch Logs (retention, KMS, data protection, deletion protection, metric filters, subscription filters, export to S3, Logs Insights, Live Tail, anomaly detection), vended logs; CloudTrail (event history, event types, trails, organization trail, multi-Region, integrity validation, encryption, S3 bucket policy, SNS, CloudWatch Logs integration, long-term retention, Lake closure); X-Ray (concepts, sampling, daemon and SDK, OpenTelemetry, integrations); the observability family in one sentence each; the decisions CloudTrail vs CloudWatch vs Config and CloudWatch vs Managed Prometheus and Grafana; the three recognise-only cards (Health Dashboard, Managed Grafana, Managed Service for Prometheus); Well-Architected guidance; Callvale's decision facts (d048 lists them); one or two case studies. Kinds: behavior, capability, restriction, default, decision, case-study.
watch: Default EC2 metrics (d021): the exam fact 'memory and disk space need the CloudWatch agent' must be grounded in a sentence that says it; if no saved page says it verbatim, narrow the claim to what the agent collects and mark the negative not-found. Never write it from memory.

Alarm actions (d024): EC2 recover and the other EC2 actions have conditions (instance types, EBS-backed, a metric of the instance): quote them with the action. Composite alarms can take fewer action types than metric alarms: quote what the page lists.
Missing data (d023): name the default treatment only from a sentence that says it is the default.

Export to S3 vs subscription filter (d032): export is a batch task and the page says how long until data can be exported; subscription filters are the real-time path. Keep both conditions in the claims.

CloudTrail defaults (d034 to d036): 'event history is enabled by default', 'trails log management events by default', 'data events are not logged by default' and 'log files are encrypted with SSE-S3 by default' are separate claims; each needs its own sentence with the word default (or narrow the claim).

Organization trail (d036): reuse organizations-org-trail-* facts for 'members cannot modify or delete'; add the CloudTrail guide facts on who can create it (management account or delegated administrator) and where logs go only if the existing facts do not cover them.
Network activity events vs VPC Flow Logs (d035): the CloudTrail FAQ #40 answer is the discriminator; quote it whole (FAQ lens may already hold it: check `facts list --service cloudtrail`).

Decision guides (d041, d042): quote one table row with its header (facts adopt --table/--row); a decision fact says 'the decision guide recommends' and never turns a guide sentence into a universal rule.
X-Ray and ALB (d039): the load balancer adds a trace header but does not send data to X-Ray: quote the sentence; do not generalise to NLB.
Well-Architected (d028, d047): guidance, not rules: claims say 'AWS recommends' or 'the Reliability Pillar recommends'.

Cards (d043 to d045): 4 to 6 facts each; prefer the 'what is' sentence and one discriminator (Health: account-specific vs public events; Grafana: IAM Identity Center or SAML users, data sources; Prometheus: PromQL and container metrics, managed collectors).
Callvale story values (6 hours, 7 years, last Tuesday) are story data, never facts; d048 lists the AWS facts each reason cites. The story never teaches a fact.
Case studies (d049): use only Wix, Phillips 66, Stripe, Choice Hotels, Wiz (ZS Associates is a listing page). Quotes at most 25 words; the fact goes under the service the quote names.

faq.job: Quick-fire FAQ facts for the FAQ section (verbatim FAQ answers, one or two sentences each): the questions listed in d050 (CloudWatch), d051 (X-Ray and APM, a section of the CloudWatch FAQ), d052 (CloudTrail) and d053 (Managed Grafana and Managed Service for Prometheus). Each fact quotes the answer sentence(s) whole; the claim keeps the answer's conditions. Kinds: behavior, capability, restriction, decision, limit.
watch: The FAQ lists (work files faq-cloudwatch.txt, faq-cloudtrail.txt, faq-grafana.txt, faq-prometheus.txt) give the question numbers used in the demand items; the last item of each list is an empty 'NA' entry, skip it.

FAQ answers can be older than the guide (CloudTrail delivery times, CloudWatch Logs agent details, Container Insights 'Public Beta' wording): when a FAQ number disagrees with a quota or guide page, the numbers lens adds the guide value; record the conflict in the demand note and do not add the FAQ number as a competing fact.

Before adding a FAQ fact for a number already covered by the numbers lens, check `facts list --service <key>`; the FAQ lens adds the quick-fire sentence only when it states something new or states it in a form the FAQ section quotes.
The CloudWatch FAQ has an Omni section (#41 to #49): skip it (not examinable yet).

rules: Quote from page snapshots only; full.md hits are pointers.
A demand item becomes filled, contradicted (with what the page says) or not-found.
Current truth comes from the guide, quota and pricing pages; What's New pages and history rows give dates and deltas only.
Files of 10 to 25 facts; every quote verbatim and complete for its claim; `--by mine-37-<lens>`.
Never refresh a cached page; fetch only pages that are not yet in the corpus.
